bibliographic.title: Feasibility of a multi-metric framework for evaluating patient-facing AI communication in cosmetic dentistry: an exploratory proof-of-concept study
bibliographic.authors: Alaa Al-Haddad, Omar Al-Karadsheh, Yazan Hassona
bibliographic.citation_apa: Al-Haddad, A., Al-Karadsheh, O., & Hassona, Y. (2026). Feasibility of a multi-metric framework for evaluating patient-facing AI communication in cosmetic dentistry: An exploratory proof-of-concept study. Frontiers in Oral Health, 7, 1837073. https://doi.org/10.3389/froh.2026.1837073

methodology.method_family: comparative benchmarking with expert human evaluation
methodology.sample_description: 80-prompt test set across four cosmetic dentistry domains; 160 responses from CSA-GPT and ChatGPT5.2; two board-certified specialists independently evaluated all responses
methodology.technology_context: patient-facing large language models; instruction-configured assistant (CSA-GPT) versus general-purpose baseline (ChatGPT5.2); conversational agents for health education and treatment explanations

eligibility.decision_rationale: The study empirically benchmarks patient-facing LLM communication quality in cosmetic dentistry using a multi-metric rubric and clinical safety audit, which is relevant to governed conversational outputs in healthcare. However, governance is referenced as a future application rather than being the primary object of study; the core contribution is an exploratory evaluation framework feasibility proof rather than operational conversational governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only partial front matter and excerpted pages were supplied; confirm full-text coverage of governance, oversight, and implementation claims before final inclusion tier.

appraisal.notes: Exploratory proof-of-concept with transparent statistical comparisons and stated need for external validation; ethics/reflexivity not evidenced in supplied excerpts.

cerqual.explanation: Findings are internally coherent and statistically reported, but the design is exploratory, domain-specific, and authors state psychometric refinement and broader testing are needed before informing governance or implementation.

coding.theme: Evaluation of patient-facing LLM communication quality
coding.subtheme: Cosmetic dentistry benchmarking and safety messaging
concepts: major factual errors and critical omissions audit
rq_alignment: evaluation frameworks for governed conversational outputs
risk and safety in regulated healthcare LLM use

synthesis.main_claim: An instruction-configured LLM (CSA-GPT) significantly outperformed a general-purpose baseline (ChatGPT5.2) on patient-facing communication metrics in cosmetic dentistry without increasing major factual errors, supporting feasibility of a multi-metric benchmarking approach.
synthesis.contribution: Provides an exploratory 20-point, theory-informed rubric and clinical safety audit for reproducible benchmarking of readability, practicality, empathetic tone, structural clarity, and safety messaging in patient-facing LLM outputs.
synthesis.limitations: Exploratory proof-of-concept requiring psychometric refinement, external validation, and broader testing before approaches can inform governance or implementation.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for evaluation metrics, safety disclaimers, and communication-quality governance prerequisites in regulated patient-facing LLM systems; not primary evidence for operational conversational governance architectures.

evidence.claim: Study addresses patient-facing LLMs in healthcare including conversational agents
evidence.excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into patient-facing healthcare applications, including conversational agents used for health education, treatment explanations, and preliminary decision support

evidence.claim: Core design is comparative benchmarking of two LLM configurations
evidence.excerpt: This proof-of-concept comparative benchmarking study used a consolidated 80-prompt test set derived from thematic analysis of real-world patient inquiries and cross-LLM synthesis

evidence.claim: Evaluation includes ethical disclaimers and clinical safety audit
evidence.excerpt: Two board-certified specialists independently evaluated all responses using a theory-informed, exploratory 20-point rubric assessing readability (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, FKGL), ethical disclaimer inclusion, practicality, empathetic tone, and structural clarity. A separate clinical safety audit assessed major factual errors and critical omissions.

evidence.claim: Instruction-configured model outperformed baseline on communication metrics
evidence.excerpt: CSA-GPT outperformed ChatGPT5.2 across all evaluated communication metrics. Mean total rubric score was 17.95 ± 1.62 for CSA-GPT vs. 9.55 ± 1.94 for ChatGPT5.2 (p < 0.001; Cohen’s d = 3.22).

evidence.claim: Mandatory disclaimers were fully present in configured model outputs
evidence.excerpt: Mandatory disclaimers were present in 100% of CSA-GPT

evidence.claim: Authors position benchmarking as potentially informing future governance after validation
evidence.excerpt: highlighting the need for psychometric refinement, external validation, and broader testing before such approaches can inform governance or implementation.

evidence.claim: Study rejects null hypotheses favoring configured model across domains
evidence.excerpt: The findings reject the null hypotheses: the configured model significantly outperformed the baseline across all measured dimensio

evidence.claim: Prior chatbot evaluations in dentistry show communication shortcomings
evidence.excerpt: Studies of orthodontic and aligner-based treatments have identified limitations in chatbot-generated responses, including variability in accuracy, structure, and patient appropriateness

evidence.claim: Communication quality should be evaluated beyond accuracy alone
evidence.excerpt: this challenge is not limited to whether AI-generated content is factually acceptable, but also whether it is communicated in a manner that is understandable, usable, and appropriately bounded for patient decision-

evidence.claim: Exploratory benchmarking may inform future governance strategies pending validation
evidence.excerpt: This highlights the need for exploratory benchmarking approaches that may inform future governance strategies, provided they undergo formal validation.
